messages:
jamie: Heads-up — hit a small production mini-surge on a 2k-seq job yesterday. Prefetch + kernel fallback path pushed KV footprint up and we started soft-shedding batches to avoid OOM.

anika: Ugh. Which tenant / model? any quick perf numbers? :eyes:

jamie: model: gpt-open-6b (quantized), tenant: sandbox-qa. Quick profiler snapshot: kernel_switch_count x3 vs baseline, p50 latency +12ms, p95 +120ms during the window. KV memory went from ~68% -> 82% over ~30s.

kevin: can you paste the scrubbed log block? curious about token budgets and admission decisions.

jamie: sure, here's the relevant slice:```
[2026-03-16T03:12:09Z] batch_id=0x7f12 prefetch_tokens=32 token_budget_target=2048 queue_wait_ms=8 kv_mem_pct=0.682 kernel_path=fast
[2026-03-16T03:12:09Z] batch_id=0x7f13 prefetch_tokens=32 token_budget_target=2048 queue_wait_ms=9 kv_mem_pct=0.715 kernel_path=fast
[2026-03-16T03:12:10Z] batch_id=0x7f14 prefetch_tokens=32 token_budget_target=2048 queue_wait_ms=11 kv_mem_pct=0.748 kernel_path=slow_fallback
[2026-03-16T03:12:11Z] batch_id=0x7f15 prefetch_tokens=32 token_budget_target=2048 queue_wait_ms=14 kv_mem_pct=0.812 kernel_path=slow_fallback shed_reason=kv_headroom
```

maddy: that kv_mem_pct ramp looks nasty. Prefetch doubling the live KV by ~15-20%? Did prefetch warm keys that triggered larger shard resident sets?

jamie: yeah, looks like prefetch pulled in many long-context KV entries; a few requests had long prefix repeats so caches accumulated. Also kernel fallback increases per-token memory for KV buffers.

anika: two levers to consider: shrink prefetch window (32->16) and add soft backoff when kv_mem_pct > 0.72 to stop admitting prefetch-heavy batches. Also maybe lower token_budget_target for that queue.

kevin: agree. From profiling, kernel fallback path allocates ephemeral shadow buffers ~= +6% per active KV slot. If we reduce prefetch from 32->16 we reduce both memory and chance of fallback.

maddy: can we implement a quick admission rule: if kv_mem_pct >= 0.72 then cap prefetch_tokens=8 and reduce token_budget_target by 25% for experimental queue? That would be a low-risk config tweak.

sre-oncall: also add a short-circuit metric alert: if kernel_switch_count spike AND kv_mem_pct > 0.75 then page oncall. We had no alert during the window.

jamie: good call. I'll push a canary change to staging with these three tweaks: prefetch 32->16 (primary), prefetch_cap_at_0.72 -> 8, token_budget_target *0.75 when kv_mem_pct>0.72. Tagging traces with "mini_surge_prefetch_v1".

infra-bot: deploy queued for canary-staging, id=deploy-20260316-1187, owner=jamie. Expected rollout: 5% nodes for 30m.

kevin: for perf regression hunting, also capture L2 cache misses and GPU memory fragmentation (if any) during canary. Add trace fields: kernel_switch_count, kv_mem_pct, admission_decision, prefetch_tokens, token_budget_target.

maddy: i'll run a synthetic 2k-seq workload against canary at 2am PST and watch KV headroom. Will report back.

anika: if canary looks good, follow-up: consider a longer-term change to delay prefetch until kernel path stable (i.e., defer prefetch until after kernel selection if fallback probability estimated high). That avoids the double-alloc problem.

jamie: notes for follow-up perf eval: create two A/B buckets — immediate prefetch vs deferred-prefetch — measure p95 and kv_mem_pct over 1M tokens. Also collect kernel-switch heatmap.

maddy: ack. will post canary results here. :thumbsup:

kevin: nice plan. TL;DR: short-term config canary (prefetch shrink + backoff + token budget cap) + alerts + richer traces, medium-term: deferred prefetch around kernel-fallback probability.

jamie: thanks everyone. I'll update the rollout doc and link traces once deploy finishes.

maddy: canary finished: no page, kv_mem_pct peaks at 71%, p95 back within normal range. I'll attach perf dump in a follow-up thread. :relieved:
